cohort: 15,156 women who delivered a singleton liveborn
finding: Significant differences in perinatal outcomes were observed between Pacific Islander and White women, with all Pacific Islander groups exhibiting an increased risk of hypertension, and variations in outcomes such as low birth weight, macrosomia, and cesarean delivery rates among different Pacific Islander subgroups.
mod_finding: Micronesian women had the highest risk of cesarean delivery among all the Pacific Islander subgroups.
